catholic church in ireland will take place on this saturday, 17th october 2026 at the city north hotel, gormanston, co. meath. delegates from every diocese across the country will gather to consider proposals, engage in communal discernment, and make practical recommendations for the church in ireland. this assembly marks a key moment in the irish synodal pathway, which began in 2021. the theme is the living out of our baptism, and discussions will focus on seven priorities: belonging, co-responsibility and lay ministry, family, formation and catechesis, healing, women, and youth. the working document, entitled “is not this what god asks of you?”, has been published and is available to read. everyone is warmly invited to pray with it and reflect on the guestion that has guided the synodal pathway from the beginning: “what does god want from the church in ireland at this time?”. we ask all parishioners to keep this important gathering in your prayers. a weekend like no other: catholic marriage encounter weekend at st. mary's, knock, co. mayo from friday 9th to sunday 11th april 2027. this residential weekend starts at 7.30pm on friday and finishes at 4.30pm on sunday, and is open to all married couples. online booking only at

missionaries. please be generous to this appeal. october, safeguarding month-speaking up: being attentive to the wellbeing and safety of children and young people is an important part of safeguarding. wave of light at the abbey: on october 15th, buildings across ireland plan to join the global wave of light and to light up blue and pink to mark pregnancy and infant loss remembrance day.
to m ark the event, with the co-operation of the opw and local politicians, quin abbey is set to be illumin ated in blue and pink.
at 7pm, people are asked to take a moment in memory of all the babies who are loved, m issed and never forgotten.

the event is being promoted by féileacáin, the national non-profit charity in ireland that provides support, resources, and counselling to families affected by the death of a baby around the time of birth or perinatal loss.

. sunday the 11th of october is prisoners sunday: on this sunday we pray for those in prison, for their families and for the victims of their crime.
below is the killaloe diocesan prayer for prisoners: we pray your grace lord jesus for prisoners, and their families who walk their sentence with their loved ones.

we pray you healing lord for the trauma that has caused them to hurt themselves, their families, and their victims we pray they will turn to you and begin their journey of recovery, finding compassionate support in our christian society jesus we trust in you.
